newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran awards Balal oilfield to Canadian-U.K. venture. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iran awards Balal oilfield to Canadian-U.K. venture. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]

text.p: Iran has awarded a Canadian-U.K. joint venture a contract to develop its offshore Balal oilfield, a senior official at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) said on Friday.

NIOC's board of directors had approved the Balal contract to Canadian independent oil firm Bow Valley and U.K. privately-owned Pell Frischmann Engineering Limited, said the official who declined to be named. (Corrects headline and text to make clear Pell Frischmann is a U.K.-based company and not Swiss-based).
The official told Reuters that the field had 80 million barrels of crude reserves which had the potential to produce between 35,000 and 40,000 barrels per day.
"The NIOC board recently approved the contract," the official told Reuters.

Balal is the second oilfield Iran has awarded to foreign firms under its "buy-back" formula launched in 1995. It follows on NIOC's agreement with French oil firm Total to develop the Sirri E and A fields.

Under Washington's Iran-Libya sanctions act signed by U.S. President Bill Clinton last year, non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million dollars or more a year in Iran or Libya's oil and gas sectors are vulnerable to a range of sanctions.
The value of the Balal deal was was not immediately available.
